recorded_via: a real Qwen Code CLI session (0.23.0), pointed at the capture proxy via ~/.qwen/settings.json (model/@lane suffix, not the ignis-bench record --class marker header)
purpose: supplementary: exercising the capture proxy against a genuine agent client, not the shape-bearing G4 trace (bench/traces/g4-load-trace.jsonl is that). Kept as a second artifact because it is real evidence of a different question than the scripted session answers.
note: 83 requests over ~13.2 minutes of real interactive use. No corruption, no error/warn/panic in the reference's log across the whole session -- the capture proxy's byte-for-byte SSE forwarding held up against a real client (this ticket's 'tool-call/thinking-stream damage' criterion: none observed, nothing to file). Model-id tags actually sent: 56x '@classifier', 27x '@main', 0x '@agents' -- confirms the user's own observation live: Qwen Code's subagent/explore path (configured to route through the '@agents' lane, agents.builtin.exploreModel / modelGrades.agents in settings.json) never fired a single request in this session, despite the main+classifier lanes working end to end (config -> capture proxy -> pinned reference, all healthy). The gap is client-side subagent orchestration not invoking its configured model at all, not a proxy or reference defect -- out of #118's scope to diagnose further; noted here as the concrete evidence for the ticket. Seven distinct system-prompt roles were seen across the session (main CLI agent, plus Qwen Code's own housekeeping calls: memory extraction, memory selection, a 'memory dream' reflective pass, chat-title generation, tool-call summary labels, and a security classifier) -- real client traffic is shaped very differently from a scripted 'N coding subagents' burst, which is exactly why this is kept as a separate, clearly-labeled artifact rather than folded into the shape-bearing trace.
